title: Free producer build before checks; keep failed check output tails
summary: Goal: stop the job holding two builds during checks, and make failed checks diagnosable for retries and people. Remove the producer's build directory before checks start (keeping the candidate work tree), then save each failed check's last 200 output lines in the job's records and print failing test names in the drain log.

defaults_applied.how: New tests plus cargo test and clippy -D warnings criteria.
Behavior criteria exercised by running cargo test.
Criteria check the directory is gone and the output tail recorded, not wiring.
Removes the build before checks rather than raising the disk allowance.
One focused change in the named files.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs (CheckRun exec at line 20, baseline checks with athena_agent::env::build), crates/athena-core/src/state.rs (existing test removing_the_producer_build_directory_keeps_the_rest_of_target), crates/athena-agent/src/env.rs (per-job build directories), crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (existing low-disk tests that remove build dirs before checks). Entry: drain dispatches the job, the producer runs, then the checks stage runs; the removal must go between producer end and the first check. Record allow-list: if the output tail is stored as a new record or data file, the producer must find the validation covering it (check_record_file, AnyRecord or its round-trip test) and extend it; preferably it extends an existing record. The tail is measured directly from the real check output captured by the checks path, not a stand-in.
Reuses the existing helper that removes the producer build directory in crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs and state.rs rather than adding new deletion logic.
Failing test names are parsed from cargo test output lines like 'test x::y ... FAILED' and printed in the drain log line; falls back to the check name if none parse.
Audience: people and automated retries reading the drain log and job records.
No rule is added that refuses readings, so no refusal-rate criterion applies.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a new test through the real checks path (not a unit stub) asserts the producer's build directory does not exist when the first check starts and the candidate's work tree still exists afterwards.

Run cargo test: a new test with a deliberately failing check asserts the drain log line contains the failing test name (not just 'test FAILED') and the job's committed records contain the last 200 lines of that check's output (a longer output is truncated to its final 200 lines).

git diff shows the CHANGELOG.md entry describing both changes, and changes limited to crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs, crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs, crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, tests, and CHANGELOG.md (plus any record type needed).
Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test: all pass.
Run cargo test: existing drain tests for low disk and interrupted-job reclaim still pass, showing the work tree and candidate are kept.

out_of_scope: Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, or workflow files
Changing disk allowance sizes or thresholds
Reworking how checks build in their own directory
Retry policy changes based on the recorded output
departures: Slightly higher cost: touches the checks pipeline, records, and drain log with two new tests through the real path.
urgent_reason: Cuts wasted time: disk exhaustion mid-test causes failed attempts and retries, and unrecorded failure output forces redo-work retries.
hard_reason: It changes the run pipeline's checks stage and what job records hold, where a mistake could lose the candidate or hide failures.
